definitions.explanation: To receive something that is given, sent, or directed toward you. Often used for abstract things like impressions, influence, or damage.
To undergo or sit for an exam, test, interview, or medical examination.

definitions.gloss: to be popular, to be well-received (colloquial)
definitions.explanation: In casual speech, to be funny or successful with an audience. Often used as ウケる in katakana.

examples.japanese: {来週|らいしゅう}{試験|しけん}を{受|う}けます。
examples.english: I will take an exam next week.
examples.notes: {試験|しけん}を{受|う}ける is the standard expression for 'take a test'

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{大|おお}きな{影響|えいきょう}を{受|う}けた。
examples.english: He received a big influence. / He was greatly influenced.
examples.notes: {影響|えいきょう}を{受|う}ける = to be influenced

examples.japanese: {面接|めんせつ}を{受|う}けに{行|い}く。
examples.english: I'm going to have an interview.

examples.japanese: {台風|たいふう}で{大|おお}きな{被害|ひがい}を{受|う}けた。
examples.english: We suffered major damage from the typhoon.
examples.notes: {被害|ひがい}を{受|う}ける = to suffer damage

examples.japanese: その{冗談|じょうだん}、すごくウケた！
examples.english: That joke was a big hit!

examples.japanese: {印象|いんしょう}を{受|う}けた。
{注目|ちゅうもく}を{受|う}けている。
{手術|しゅじゅつ}を{受|う}けた。
{入学|にゅうがく}{試験|しけん}を{受|う}けた。
{授業|じゅぎょう}を{受|う}ける。
その{話|はなし}はウケるよ。
examples.english: That story will go over well.

examples.japanese: {若者|わかもの}にウケている。
この{映画|えいが}は{海外|かいがい}でもウケた。
examples.english: This movie was a hit overseas too.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{物真似|ものまね}はいつもクラスでウケている。
examples.english: His impressions are always a hit in class.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: {他動詞|たどうし} (transitive). Pattern: Xを{受|う}ける (receive/take X). No intransitive pair.

ASPECT: ている indicates ongoing state or completed action with continuing relevance. {受|う}けている = 'is receiving/undergoing' or 'has received.'

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{試験|しけん}を{受|う}ける (take an exam)
・{面接|めんせつ}を{受|う}ける (have an interview)
・{影響|えいきょう}を{受|う}ける (be influenced)
・{被害|ひがい}を{受|う}ける (suffer damage)
・{印象|いんしょう}を{受|う}ける (receive an impression)
・{手術|しゅじゅつ}を{受|う}ける (undergo surgery)

NUANCE: Unlike もらう (to receive from someone), {受|う}ける often implies receiving something abstract or undergoing an experience. For concrete gifts, もらう is more natural.

COLLOQUIAL: ウケる (often in katakana) means 'to be funny/popular.' {彼|かれ}の{話|はなし}がウケた = 'His story went over well.'
